text:
Cole Hutson was the 43rd pick in 2024, and 19 games into his rookie season he has 15 points, five of them on the power play. Defensemen picked in his range score a median 0.21 points a game in their first real season; he's at 0.79. The headlines have started comparing him with his brother Lane, who won the Calder in Montreal.

The interesting part is how he does it. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in six games, has 33% of his setups going across the royal road, against 6% for a typical defenseman: the pass that drags a goalie side to side. His ice time is climbing too, to 20:18 over his last ten from 19:36 on the season.

Some of the points will settle. Our range for his scoring rate sits a little under where he is now, and his 12% shooting is about twice what defensemen usually manage. He also doesn't sound satisfied: after a stretch with an overtime winner and a highlight assist, RMNB's headline had him saying "I'm just not playing well enough." Washington has lost four straight; he had three assists in one of them.
